page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard1.2 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the first-generation Standard family. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon E5-2699 v3 processor clocked at a base frequency of 2.3 GHz. The instance configuration provides 4 vCPUs backed by 2 dedicated physical cores with hyperthreading enabled at 2 threads per core, alongside 14.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of 3.5 GB of RAM per vCPU.

This server instance contains no integrated local NVMe storage and includes no discrete graphics processing hardware, requiring all persistent data volumes to be mounted externally via network-attached block storage. Network connectivity features one complimentary public IPv4 address for external ingress and egress routing.

From an architectural standpoint, the Intel Xeon E5-2699 v3 processor represents a legacy hardware profile. While dedicated physical cores avoid the resource contention typical of burstable or shared hypervisors, the generation lacks contemporary instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AMX extensions. Workload throughput is therefore constrained by older per-core instructions and lower memory bandwidth relative to modern server platforms.

The 1:3.5 CPU-to-memory ratio provides a balanced baseline suitable for horizontal web serving, lightweight application backends, dev-test environments, and standard middle-tier enterprise services that do not depend on specialized vector processing, high memory density, or low-latency local NVMe scratch space.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard1.2 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2699 v3 processor clocked at 2.3 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 4 vCPUs mapped across 2 dedicated physical cores with 2 threads per core, complemented by 14.0 GB of system memory at 3.5 GB per vCPU. It includes zero GPU accelerators and provides no onboard local storage, necessitating reliance on remote block storage for persistence. Network configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Given its dedicated core allocation and balanced compute-to-memory profile, VM.Standard1.2 operates as a cost-effective platform for standard utility workloads, development environments, middle-tier enterprise applications, and general web services that do not require modern vector acceleration or high-speed local disk storage.
